summary: Contestants develop a comprehensive business plan and operating strategy for a new venture or startup, then prepare and present an investor-ready pitch to secure financing. The event includes a written business plan submission and an oral presentation, plus a certification exam at the National Leadership Conference.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes setup
No less than five (5) and no more than seven (7) minutes oral presentation, including the pitch to the investors
No more than five (5) minutes judges’ questions
No more than fifty (50) minutes for certification test
submission_requirements: One combined PDF file containing Business Plan, Title Page, Table of Contents, Works Cited formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form
Contestant ID is required for all submissions
Materials from non-registered contestants and/or those missing Contestant ID cannot be accepted
Business Plan must not exceed ten (10) pages single-sided; Title Page, Table of Contents, and Works Cited are not included in the ten (10) page limit
Business Plan must follow the Business Plan format (Sections I-VIII) in the Style & Reference Manual
Business Plan, including Title Page, Table of Contents, and Works Cited must be formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual
Contestant is responsible for securing a signed BPA Release Form(s) from any person, including oneself, whose image or work is used in the project
Contestant is responsible for citing all sources, including oneself, on the Works Cited page for any work used on the project
Materials must follow the organization’s BPA Graphic Standards and make proper use of the BPA logo and/or organization’s name
presubmit_items: Business Plan in one combined PDF to include: Title Page, Table of Contents, Business Plan, Works Cited, BPA Release Form(s), AI Usage and Documentation Form
deadlines: National Deadline: April 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
what_to_bring: Supporting materials (e.g., research charts, brochures, etc.) for each round of presentations
One single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for presentation
Optional: Product displays and props (product samples and promotional items), prepared posters, flip charts, easels, or graphs in presentation
competencies: Develop a comprehensive business plan that demonstrates understanding of entrepreneurship, feasibility, and startup requirements
Communicate research clearly and professionally in both written and oral formats
Identify and use internal and external resources that support business development and planning
Identify and analyze target customer groups, demographics, and customer relationship needs
Develop and justify pricing strategies based on customer value, costs, and competition
Prepare and justify the loan amount and financial data needed to establish the business, including startup costs and basic financial projections
Deliver clear, persuasive, and informative presentations that effectively communicate the business concept

rubric.criterion: Contestant followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.
Business Plan did not exceed ten (10) pages single-sided. The Title Page, Table of Contents, and Works Cited are not included in the ten (10) page limit.

Contestant submitted one (1) combined PDF file containing their Business Plan to include the Title Page, Table of Contents, Works Cited formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form.
Management and Ownership of the Business

rubric.description: In-depth analysis, strong edge, justified pricing.
Plan is exceptionally well-organized, concise, and complete.
Contains very few or no grammar or spelling errors.

rubric.criterion: Contestant followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy

rubric.description: Contestant maintains good eye contact, uses appropriate gestures and body language, and varies their tone and pace adequately.
Presentation content flows adequately, with a mostly clear structure and smooth transitions between points.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.
Setup lasted no longer than three (3) minutes, and the presentation lasted no less than five (5) and no more than seven (7) minutes.

judging_notes: AI Policy Level 2 Permitted with Citation
Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the contestants and take place within the time allotted
No Internet access will be provided on-site at the NLC; however, contestants may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
No materials may be left with the judges
At NLC, contestants will take the Entrepreneurship and Small Business (ESB) certification exam. Contestants passing this certification will have 50 points added to their event score.
Reference materials are not allowed for certification testing
Finals may be part of the competition
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
Presentation will be stopped at seven (7) minutes
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this judged event
Contestants must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked
Entries that do not follow the provided topic or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy will be disqualified
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
